sources.entry: Notchi - Turn the MacBook notch into a place to ask AI, save notes, set reminders, or run coding agents.

summary.one_liner: Notchi is a macOS menu-bar app that puts an AI assistant in the MacBook notch area for asking questions, saving notes, setting reminders, and handing projects to coding agents.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a menu-bar app built in Liquid Glass that lets you ask an AI questions from the notch, with web search used when needed. Follow-up questions keep the last answer visible above the prompt, and all questions share a unified conversation thread with continuous memory and history. A slash menu saves notes and reminders, and lines with a time are sent to Reminders. It can render numbers as charts, and it can hand a project off to Codex, Claude Code or Cursor. An Audit view in Settings lists every request Notchi sends. The README says chats and memory are stored locally on the Mac, that no sign-up is required, and that you can connect your own model provider key directly.
use_cases: ask an AI assistant from the menu bar
save quick notes on a Mac
hand a coding project to Codex or Claude Code
audit what data an AI app sends
notable: Lives in the MacBook notch as a menu-bar app
Unified conversation thread with continuous memory
Bring-your-own model provider key, with an Audit log of every request
Lines with a time are sent to Reminders
Can hand projects to Codex, Claude Code or Cursor agents
caveats: macOS only, installed via Homebrew cask
README links to a Pricing page, so some paid tier appears to exist (details not in the README)
